The concentration of free calcium ions \([Ca^{2+}]\) in a solution of 0.02 M stoichiometric Ca-EDTA complex can be determined from the dissociation equilibrium. The formation constant is \(K_f = 5 \times 10^{10}\), so the dissociation constant is \(K_d = 1/K_f = 2 \times 10^{-11}\).

The dissociation reaction is:  
\[
CaY^{2-} \rightleftharpoons Ca^{2+} + Y^{4-}
\]

Let \([Ca^{2+}] = [Y^{4-}] = x\), and \([CaY^{2-}] \approx 0.02 - x \approx 0.02\) M (since \(x\) will be very small).

\[
K_d = \frac{[Ca^{2+}][Y^{4-}]}{[CaY^{2-}]} = \frac{x^2}{0.02} = 2 \times 10^{-11}
\]

\[
x^2 = 0.02 \times 2 \times 10^{-11} = 4 \times 10^{-13}
\]

\[
x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 2 \times 10^{-6.5} \approx 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ M}
\]

Thus, the concentration of calcium ions is \(6.3 \times 10^{-7}\) M, corresponding to option (D). The proposed answer of "2" (Option B) is incorrect.
